whatIsSection.title: What Is
whatIsSection.subtitle: Bad breath, also known as halitosis, is persistent unpleasant odor from the mouth. While occasional bad breath may follow certain foods, chronic bad breath often signals an underlying oral health issue that needs professional treatment.

whyMattersBox.paragraph: Persistent bad breath may be caused by several underlying factors. Early diagnosis helps prevent more serious dental problems while restoring fresh breath.

items.title: Gum Disease

items.title: Dry Mouth
items.description: Reduced saliva flow allows odor-causing bacteria to thrive.

items.title: Tongue Bacteria
items.description: A coated tongue harbors bacteria that produce persistent odor.

items.question: What causes persistent bad breath?
items.answer: Persistent bad breath is commonly caused by poor oral hygiene, gum disease, plaque buildup, tooth decay, dry mouth, tongue bacteria, or dental infections.

items.question: Can bad breath be permanently treated?
items.answer: Yes. Once the underlying cause is identified and treated, many patients experience long-lasting improvement with proper oral hygiene and regular dental check-ups.

items.question: Is bad breath always caused by dental problems?
items.answer: Not always. While oral health issues are the most common cause, some medical conditions can also contribute. A dental evaluation helps determine whether further medical assessment is needed.

items.question: Is professional cleaning helpful for bad breath?
items.answer: Yes. Professional dental cleaning removes plaque, tartar, and bacteria that are often responsible for chronic bad breath.

items.question: How much does bad breath treatment cost in Pune?
items.answer: The cost varies depending on the underlying cause and the treatment required. A consultation allows us to provide an accurate estimate.

items.question: How can I prevent bad breath?
items.answer: Maintaining good oral hygiene, brushing twice daily, flossing, cleaning your tongue, staying hydrated, and scheduling regular dental check-ups can significantly reduce the risk of bad breath.
